messages.author: e00d1783b2eb0abc
messages.subject: Animals avoiding transects... as usual
parts:
Hi there!
I am currently helping to analyze a survey conducted along hunting
trails. I suspect animals (in our case birds) to have avoided hunting
trails and / or distances seemed to have been measured poorly /
inaccurate. I would like to inquire on any means to filter the data
(sort of a noise filtering of data to estimate the proportion of animals
missed close to the line, maybe based upon the "overloaded" next
distance bin) before we do the actual analysis. I'm cool with R,
however, I have not yet dug into the statistical analysis and
preparation of survey data outside of distance. Any suggestions on how
to improve our analysis? I attached the binning resulting from of a very
basic and quick analysis I just ran for illustration.


BTW: It is sort of annoying that the results window on my win7 pc is
half way between minimized and maximized, if you get what I mean? I've
tried to attach a screenshot that may be more congruent in its
intentions, but, as I could have expected, there isno place for image
attachments on a mailing list. I could still provide you with a
screenshot of the situation. I even drew arrows on it. :) I strongly
suspect win7 to be the problem (my personal experience with microsoft OS
rejects any other H0), but anyway, it is not that terrible (since you
just have to click on minimize, then maximize again to restore its window)!
